properties.areaDesc: San Luis Obispo County Beaches; Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 4 at 3:29PM PST until November 5 at 7:00AM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Large breaking waves of 8 to 11 ft with dangerous rip
currents.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...Until 7 AM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large
breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and
rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Additional High Surf Advisories and Coastal
Flood Advisories may be needed in the near future.
properties.instruction:
Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

NWSheadline: HIGH SURF ADVISORY IN EFFECT UNTIL 7 AM PST THURSDAY

properties.areaDesc: San Diego County Coastal Areas; Orange County Coastal
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 4 at 12:42PM PST until November 10 at 12:00PM PST by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Minor to locally moderate coastal flooding expected.
Additionally, dangerous rip currents and surf of 3 to 5 feet
expcted along west-facing beaches.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County
Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...From 4 AM Friday to noon PST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Coastal residents and managers of
infrastructure in the advisory area should prepare for rising
water and take appropriate action to protect life and property.
Highest tides will occur in the late morning each day. Observed
high tides are 1.3 to 1.6 feet above astronomical tide
predictions. Surf will increase starting next Monday, but there
is uncertainty in details at this time.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

NWSheadline: COASTAL FLOOD ADVISORY IN EFFECT FROM 4 AM FRIDAY TO NOON PST TUESDAY

properties.headline: Frost Advisory issued November 4 at 10:54AM PST until November 5 at 9:00AM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Temperatures as low as 33 will result in frost formation.

* WHERE...Northern Mendocino Interior, Southeastern Interior
Humboldt, Northern Lake, and Western Lake.

* WHEN...From 11 PM this evening to 9 AM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Frost could harm sensitive outdoor vegetation. Sensitive
outdoor plants may be killed if left uncovered.
properties.instruction: Take steps now to protect tender plants from the cold.

NWSheadline: FROST ADVISORY IN EFFECT FROM 11 PM THIS EVENING TO 9 AM PST THURSDAY

properties.areaDesc: Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued November 4 at 10:05AM PST until November 7 at 7:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to 1.6 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards
Statement, an increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip
currents with breaking waves of 12 to 16 ft expected.

* WHERE...Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 6 AM this morning
to 1 PM PST Monday. For the Beach Hazards Statement, from 5 AM
Thursday to 7 PM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning,
pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.3 ft above normal (7.1 ft MLLW) at 8:35 AM
Thursday 11/5, 1.4 ft above normal (7.2 ft MLLW) at 9:08 AM
Friday 11/6, 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 9:38 AM
Saturday 11/7, 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 10:06 AM
Sunday 11/8, 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 10:35 AM
Monday 11/9. These predictions include up to 1.2 ft of surge
that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the
Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Stay off of jetties, piers, rocks, and other waterside
infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.
